correctness.rationale: The bridge-coset argument forces each tree edge to appear twice in a minimal full-support identity word. The fixed-point lemma on contiguous factors follows by canceling the shortest repeated pair, then observing that distinct-edge forest transpositions have cycles indexed by their support components. Leaf-edge removal, conjugation and the fixed-point lemma prove necessity and sufficiency. The independently coded product and interval criteria matched on 688,147 exhaustive words and 30,000 random longer-tree words and all contiguous factors of 347 locally noncrossing words; all order-free cases follow from the proof, not those tests.

originality.rationale: The exact all-tree word criterion was printed as Conjecture 1(iii) in Shapiro arXiv:2610.14373v1 (Oct 9 2026). The present argument settles it for arbitrary finite tree supports, not just the tabulated small cases. All database/literature comparisons made concern implications and boundary cases. The star enumerator and general moment support formula are prior work and are explicitly excluded. An undiscovered equivalence in the older genus-zero map literature remains possible.
residual_risks: Earlier equivalent tree-word criterion may be encoded implicitly in a Hurwitz/map or Coxeter normal-form theorem not identified by searches.

value.rationale: An explicit recent conjecture on genus-zero support coefficients of Cayley spectral moments is resolved with a local characterization for every tree, including trees of unbounded order and degree. The fixed-point cancellation lemma supplies structural explanation and a direct membership test, beyond routine table recomputation or star counting. The claim does not require a closed all-tree c_{2m}(T) formula.
